description: Explain the general functions and structure of a digital computer, including Computer Evolution, Performance, A Brief History of Computers.
Present an overview of the evolution of computer technology from early digital computers to the latest microprocessors, including Computer Evolution, Performance, A Brief History of Computers.
Understand the key performance issues that relate to computer design, including Computer Evolution, Performance, Designing for Performance, Performance Assessment.

Describe in detail the essential elements of computer organisation including internal bus, memory, Input/Output ( I/O) organisations and interfacing standards and discuss how these elements function;, including A Top-Level View of Computer Function, Interconnection, Computer Components, Computer Function, Bus Interconnection, Computer Memory System Overview, Elements of Cache Design, Internal Memory, External Memory.
Summarize, at a top level, the key functions of an operating system (OS), including Operating System Support, Operating System Overview.
Be able to apply Boolean algebra and digital logic to design and interpret complex digital circuits;, including Instruction Sets: Characteristics, Functions, Machine Instruction Characteristics.

Present various types of addressing modes common in instruction sets, an essential characteristics of machine instructions, types of operands supported by typical machine instruction sets, including Instruction Sets: Characteristics, Functions, Types of Operands, Instruction Sets: Characteristics, Functions, Types of Operations.
Explain processor structure and function in details, the operations of Reduced Instruction Set Computers, including Processor Structure, Function, Processor Organization.

Investigate, evaluate and communicate general trends in computing technologies such as Instruction-Level Parallelism and Superscalar Processors, including Instruction-Level Parallelism, Superscalar Processors, Symmetric Multiprocessors, Multithreading, Chip Multiprocessors.
Using AI tools and simulator tools to futher explore the main concepts, including Semiconductor Main Memory, Instruction-Level Parallelism, Superscalar Processors.
